briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. On September 15, 2026, as the specialist spokesperson for climate change, I will begin today's key climate news briefing.

sections.title: 🔴 Climate Change Skepticism and Policy Reversal Movements
sections.content: Several reports today indicate a worrying trend of climate change skepticism and policy reversals, particularly in the United States. The Trump administration characterized climate change as a 'hoax' and dismantled key environmental regulations, including repealing the core of power plant carbon regulations [1, 16, 36, 38, 195, 205, 206]. This stance has also led to the exclusion of climate change-related subjects from curricula in some U.S. universities [2], with some even noting that Democrats no longer mention 'climate change' [203]. Such political movements could pose significant obstacles to future climate action [217].

sections.title: ⚠️ Domestic and International Climate Change Damages and Crisis Warnings
sections.content: The tangible damages and threats of climate change are being severely reported both domestically and internationally. Domestically, over 95% of greenhouse farmers in the Yongin region are severely experiencing agricultural damage due to climate change, leading Yongin City to hold a meeting to devise countermeasures [5, 6, 7, 20, 24, 25, 28, 31]. Research indicating that the link between the Pacific and Indian Oceans, which had moved in tandem for the past 400 years, has been disrupted by climate change suggests fundamental changes in the marine system [8]. Internationally, record-breaking marine heatwaves are highlighting the intensified impacts of climate change [207], and scientists are warning that overlooked climate feedbacks could worsen global warming by an additional 30% by 2100 [196]. Warnings also continue that this year's Super El Niño phenomenon will lead to new extreme weather patterns and global disruption [10, 216, 219], making effective responses to climate disasters urgent [63, 67, 96].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Carbon Neutrality and Climate Response Efforts
sections.content: Amidst these crises, various efforts for carbon neutrality and climate change response are actively underway domestically. Ulsan University is pursuing academic responses by seeking international cooperation for joint climate change research with institutions such as the University of Bath and LSE in the UK [3, 13]. DL Group is making climate change response a core of its ESG management, publishing sustainability reports, and expanding new businesses such as SMRs [4, 14, 18, 19, 21, 22, 23, 29, 30, 32, 33, 34, 37]. Furthermore, cities like Gunpo and Naju have been recognized as excellent carbon-neutral local governments, receiving ministerial awards [45, 46, 47, 59, 69, 72, 74, 76, 82, 84, 85, 88, 92, 94, 98, 107, 108, 115, 117, 118], while Gwangmyeong City is investing 18 billion KRW to build a carbon-neutral smart city and expand citizen participation [41, 55, 60, 65, 66, 70, 73, 75, 77, 80, 86, 90, 97, 109, 111, 116, 120], showcasing proactive efforts at the local government level. A system to convert carbon neutrality points into local currency is being introduced in 29 regions within the year, encouraging voluntary citizen participation [39, 49, 51, 52, 53, 78, 93, 95, 102].

sections.title: 📰 Domestic Renewable Energy Policy Changes and Industry Trends
sections.content: The domestic renewable energy dissemination system has been completely overhauled after 15 years, abolishing the RPS (Renewable Portfolio Standard) and unifying it into a competitive bidding-based long-term fixed-price contract market [122, 127, 128, 129, 130, 131, 133, 134, 135, 137, 138, 143, 148, 154, 156, 158, 159, 161, 162, 166, 167, 169, 180, 184, 190]. While this is evaluated as a measure to enhance the efficiency and transparency of the renewable energy industry, concerns are also being raised about the potential for reduced investment in wind and solar power, as warned by German banks [126]. Meanwhile, the Korea Power Exchange is emphasizing the importance of ESS (Energy Storage Systems) as 'vessels for renewable energy' [124, 150, 174, 186, 193], and LS Electric and Korea Electric Power Corporation are collaborating on the development of 'grid-forming,' a next-generation power grid technology to respond to the expansion of renewable energy, seeking to build a stable power grid [145, 146, 176, 183, 189]. Jeju Island is accelerating the establishment of innovative models through renewable energy utilization, presenting a vision to leap forward as a 'climate economy capital' based on renewable energy and green hydrogen, and commencing the design for an AI transformation [125, 132, 168, 170, 172, 178, 181].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the severe reality of climate change, alongside various domestic and international efforts to overcome it. Through continued attention and cooperation, we must build a more sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
